Sacrifice

/SAC-ruh-fize/ — accent on SAC · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To sacrifice something is to give it up, often something valuable or important, for the sake of a greater goal or another person's benefit.

She sacrificed her weekend plans to help her brother move apartments.

Worked Example

A doctor realizes her research career is stalling because of hospital administrative duties. She gives up her research to focus on caring for patients in underserved communities. She sacrificed her scientific ambitions to serve those who needed her most.

'Sacrifice' is the perfect word here because it shows the doctor knowingly gave up something valuable (her research career) for a greater purpose (serving the community). 'Gave up' is too plain. 'Abandoned' sounds negative. 'Sacrificed' conveys both the cost and the purpose.

How Sacrifice Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

relinquish

relinquish: formally let go of something held

forego

forego: choose to do without something desirable

donate

donate: give away freely to help others

Antonyms

indulgence

indulgence: treating yourself to whatever you want

retain

retain: keep something instead of giving it up

How Strong Is It? — offer → yield → surrender → sacrifice

offer vs. sacrifice

offer vs. sacrifice: Offer is far weaker than sacrifice: offering means presenting something someone may take, while sacrificing means truly giving up something valuable for a greater goal.

yield vs. sacrifice

yield vs. sacrifice: Yield is weaker than sacrifice: yielding means letting go under pressure, while sacrificing means willingly giving up something precious for a purpose you believe in.

surrender vs. sacrifice

surrender vs. sacrifice: Surrender comes close to sacrifice but lacks its purpose: surrendering gives something up because you must, while sacrificing gives it up by choice for something greater.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — sacri-

Root — sacri-: sacred, holy (from Latin sacer; the -i- is the Latin linking vowel)

Root — -fice

Root — -fice: to make, do (from Latin facere)

Put it together

Put it together: Sacrifice joins sacri- (sacred, holy — from Latin sacer) with -fice (to make, do — from Latin facere): literally 'to make sacred.' Giving something up for a higher purpose sets it apart as special — which is how the word came to mean giving up what you value for a greater goal.

Use the root in a new word: sacred

Use the root in a new word: sacred: A sacred place is treated as holy and set apart — the same Latin root sacer that begins sacrifice, 'to make sacred' by giving something up.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Sacrifice is the word for giving up something genuinely valuable or important for a greater goal or someone else's benefit. If you just mean 'give away' or 'donate,' use those simpler words. Use sacrifice when the cost to yourself is real and worth noting.
